rfi.description: Icelanders will vote on Saturday on whether to resume negotiations to join the European Union, with the result expected to be finely balanced after a campaign dominated by questions of sovereignty, fishing and the country’s place in an increasingly uncertain geopolitical landscape.

rfi.title: Trapped for 115 days, cargo ship captain recounts ordeal in Strait of Hormuz
rfi.description: In late January 2026, the Banglar Joyjatra, a Bangladeshi bulk carrier, entered the Persian Gulf on what should have been a routine commercial voyage before continuing to South Africa. Instead, Captain Mohammad Shafiqul Islam and his crew became trapped for 115 days as conflict engulfed the Strait of Hormuz. He told RFI how the voyage turned into a fight to get his ship and crew safely out.

rfi.title: ‘Words and promises not enough’ as Syria’s Kurds face uncertain future
rfi.description: Syria’s Kurds are facing an uncertain future after this week’s dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces and the integration of military and civilian institutions in northeastern Syria into the Syrian state, raising questions over what the changes will mean for their rights, safety and daily lives. RFI spoke to a Kurdish civil society activist in the region.

rfi.title: Nepal’s deadly glacier collapse exposes climate risks across the Himalayas
rfi.description: A massive glacier collapse that triggered deadly flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border has exposed the growing dangers facing the rapidly warming Himalayas, where scientists say retreating ice and thawing ground are making mountain landscapes increasingly unstable.

rfi.title: Algeria mourns wildfire victims as firefighters battle deadly blazes

rfi.title: Macron to meet new UK PM Burnham against backdrop of Bayeux Tapestry
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will travel to London on Wednesday for his first meeting with the United Kingdom's new prime minister, Andy Burnham, in what will be the first visit by a European Union leader since he took office. Macron will also unveil the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum in a "significant moment" for Franco-British relations.

rfi.title: French presidential hopefuls clash over economy and EU in first debate

rfi.title: Cop17 races for desertification deal as report warns half world’s soils under threat
rfi.description: Delegates at the Cop17 summit on desertification in Mongolia are seeking to seal a deal to combat drought on Friday, the last day of the event – as a United Nations report warns the world's soils are rapidly deteriorating, while tried and tested solutions are not being implemented.

rfi.title: Looking up: French sailors ditch GPS to rediscover celestial art of navigation
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. A deux mois des élections de mi-mandat, le cadre légal du vote par correspondance aux Etats-Unis demeure flottant. Donald Trump a restreint la pratique par décret présidentiel mais les tribunaux n’ont pas rendu leur verdict, alors que les premiers bulletins doivent partir ces prochains jours

Dans quelles conditions les électeurs américains pourront-ils voter par correspondance le 3 novem

letemps.title: Roger Federer est très occupé mais aime aussi ne rien faire: «Cela me permet de réfléchir et de rester créatif»
letemps.description:
Le Bâlois sera intronisé au Hall of Fame du tennis samedi soir à Newport, dans le Rhode Island. Quatre ans après sa retraite, sa vie se partage entre vie de famille, gestion de son image de marque et de ses affaires, et moments d'introspection

spiegel.title: Audi Q6 e-tron und XPeng P7+: Deutsches und chinesisches Elektroauto im Technik-Test
spiegel.description: Chinesische Elektroautos sind günstiger als deutsche. Aber sind sie tatsächlich auch technisch überlegen? Ein Vergleichstest zwischen einem Audi und einem XPeng in fünf Disziplinen gibt Aufschluss.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Suche nach Überlebenden geht weiter, Gefahr von Seuchen steigt
spiegel.description: Dichter Nebel, Monsunregen und abgelagerter Schlamm erschweren die Suche nach Überlebenden. Weil die menschlichen Überreste von Verstorbenen zunehmend verwesen, warnen Gesundheitsexperten vor einer wachsenden Seuchengefahr.

spiegel.title: Coco Gauff: US-Tennisstar wundert sich über dreiste Ticketwünsche
spiegel.description: »Kann ich bitte acht Tickets für dein Spiel in deiner Loge haben?« Über solch absurde Anfragen rümpft Tennisprofi Coco Gauff amüsiert die Nase. Das verriet sie nach einem deutlichen Instagram-Posting ihrer Mutter.

spiegel.title: »Journey«: Platz 10 im SPIEGEL Games-Kanon
spiegel.description: Ein Berg, eine Reise, eine Partnerschaft ohne Worte: »Journey« begleitet zwei Figuren auf dem beschwerlichen Weg zu einem strahlenden Gipfel. Und verarbeitet darin ein ganzes Leben.

spiegel.title: Großglockner in Österreich: Bergführer bedrängt Alpinisten – Polizei ermittelt
spiegel.description: »Ich bin Bergführer, halt dein Maul«: Am Großglockner drängelt sich ein Bergführer vor und gerät dann mit einem anderen Bergsteiger verbal und körperlich aneinander. Nun ist die Szene in Aufruhr.

spiegel.title: 2. Bundesliga: Drei Spiele, 22 Tore – Wolfsburg, Heidenheim und Co. liefern Spektakel
spiegel.description: Turbulente Partien in der Zweiten Bundesliga: Wolfsburg dreht das Spiel dank des auch in Karlsruhe unbeliebten Fabian Reese. Heidenheim genügt eine starke Schlussphase, und Cottbus reichen selbst drei Tore nicht.

spiegel.title: »Hollow Knight«: Platz 13 im SPIEGEL Games-Kanon
spiegel.description: Ein kleiner Krieger verirrt sich in eine Welt aus schmalen, verwinkelten Tunneln, purer Finsternis und übermächtigen Gegnern. Doch wer sich einmal nach Heilandsnest wagt, will nie wieder weg.

spiegel.title: Stefan Mross: Ende der ARD-Schlagershow »Immer wieder sonntags« nach zwei Jahrzehnten
spiegel.description: Über 20 Jahre moderierte Musiker Stefan Mross die ARD-Schlagershow »Immer wieder sonntags«. Jetzt wird die Sendung nach mehr als drei Dekaden abgesetzt. Der Volksmusikstar ist enttäuscht.

spiegel.title: Beastie Boys: Erstes Album nach dem Tod von Adam Yauch - Party auf Ruinen
spiegel.description: Mehr als 14 Jahre nach dem Tod eines ihrer MCs erscheint jetzt ein neues Album von einem der Beastie Boys: Mike D bellt auf »Thank You« in bewährter Manier die Reime raus, als müsste er sie schnellstmöglich loswerden. Doch etwas fehlt.

spiegel.title: Osnabrück: Diese Rentnerin schlichtet ehrenamtlich Streit zwischen Kindern
spiegel.description: Wenn es Zoff gibt, kommen die Schülerinnen und Schüler der Grundschule Eversburg in den »Raum der guten Lösungen«. Dort helfen ihnen Menschen im Seniorenalter, sich wieder zu vertragen.

spiegel.title: FPÖ in Österreich: Was eine Regierungsbeteiligung der AfD bedeuten könnte - Podcast
spiegel.description: Die FPÖ regierte in Österreich im Bund dreimal – und scheiterte jedes Mal. Trotzdem wurde sie danach stärker und radikaler. Was ihre Geschichte für eine mögliche AfD-Regierung in Deutschland lehrt.

spiegel.title: Solarenergie: Wie die Nutzung der Sonne zur Erfolgsgeschichte wurde
spiegel.description: Vor 50 Jahren setzten Rolf Disch und Axel Mayer auf eine Energiewende, die damals völlig utopisch schien. Heute hat sich die Solarenergie durchgesetzt, aber zufrieden sind die beiden Pioniere nicht.

spiegel.title: »Nancy Grace Roman«: Neues Nasa-Teleskop wäre fast ein Spionagesatellit geworden
spiegel.description: Ein Geheimdienst lieferte den Spiegel, deutsche Forscher die Präzisionstechnik, und das Weiße Haus sorgte für Drama: Bald startet das »Nancy Grace Roman«-Teleskop, um die Suche nach Leben im All voranzubringen.

spiegel.title: Einsamkeit bei jungen Menschen: Wie es ist, als einzige Schwarze Frau im Semester zu studieren
spiegel.description: Als Romance Bassingha ihr juristisches Studium beginnt, scheinen die Freundschaften schon festzustehen. Sie fühlt sich als einzige Schwarze Person außen vor – und fragt sich: Wie sehr will ich mich anpassen, um dazuzugehören?

spiegel.title: Digitale Gewalt: CDU-Politikerinnen verlangen schärferes Gesetz
spiegel.description: Bundesjustizministerin Hubig hat im April einen Gesetzentwurf zur Verschärfung des Rechts gegen digitale Gewalt vorgelegt. Schon vor der Debatte im Parlament kommen nun Forderungen nach umfassenderem, härter durchgesetztem Schutz.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: Zehntausende nehmen Abschied von König Harald V.
spiegel.description: Sie kommen mit ihren Kindern, legen Blumen und Karten nieder: In Oslo nehmen die Menschen Abschied vom verstorbenen König Harald V. Sein Sohn Haakon VIII. dürfte sich schon bald mit einer Ansprache an die Bevölkerung wenden.

spiegel.title: New York: Fehlendes Personal soll tödliche Kollision in LaGuardia begünstigt haben
spiegel.description: Im März starben zwei Piloten bei der Kollision ihres Jets mit einem Feuerwehrauto auf dem New Yorker Flughafen LaGuardia. Erst kurz vorm Crash warnte der Tower. Hatten sich zwei Fluglotsen zu früh von der Schicht verabschiedet?

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Regierung ficht Gerichtsentscheid zur Briefwahl an
spiegel.description: Die US-Regierung zieht im Streit über geänderte Regeln zur Briefwahl vor die nächste Instanz. Kritiker werfen dem Präsidenten vor, die Stimmabgabe per Post erschweren zu wollen.

npr.title: Photos: See the aftermath of deadly flash floods in Nepal
npr.description: Nepal officials say the death toll has continues to rise in Wednesday's floods that washed away communities in Nepal and Tibet, which is held by China. About 2,500 people are missing in both areas.

npr.title: Srebrenica survivor Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death
npr.description: Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death with NPR's Scott Simon. All of Hrustanovic's adult male relatives died in the Srebrenica Massacre engineered by Mladic.

npr.title: Trump says U.S. has entered deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves
npr.description: President Trump says his administration has entered a sweeping agreement with Venezuela that could give the U.S. access to vast amounts of the South American country's untapped oil reserves, at cost.

npr.title: After 6 months of war, Iran's battered regime remains entrenched
npr.description: Instead of collapsing, the Iranian regime has dug in its heels and taken an even harder line.

npr.title: Experts warn more flooding might hit Nepal. And, Fed chairman to give key address
npr.description: As the death toll rises from flash floods that hit the Nepal-Tibet border, experts are warning more flooding could be on the way. And, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is expected to give a key address today.

npr.title: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing after flash floods in Nepal and Tibet
npr.description: Hundreds of people were killed by devastating flash floods that hit the Nepal-Tibet border, sweeping away roads, bridges and entire villages. More than 1,000 people are still missing.

npr.title: 'It's essentially been one long day': A daughter details search for parents in Nepal
npr.description: Shreya Ahuja is searching for her parents after devastating floods struck Nepal. She is calling for international help and communications access as her family waits for news.

npr.title: U.S. says pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant. Energy experts disagree
npr.description: Treasure Secretary Scott Bessent said oil pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant in two years. Energy experts say that is unlikely to happen.

npr.title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
npr.description: As the climate continues to warm, scientists warn that the frequency of disasters like the floods in Nepal will increase.

npr.title: Mike D thought making music was behind him. Then came 'Thank You'
npr.description: His first solo album finds the Beastie Boys rapper making music with his sons and embracing the unpredictability of collaboration.

nyt.title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
nyt.description: State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.

nyt.title: What’s Changing For Teens on Instagram and Facebook After Meta Settlement
nyt.description: Meta agreed to set more time limits and enhance protections in its platforms for young users, but was short on some specifics.

nyt.title: Trump Says U.S. Struck Deal for Control of More Than 65 Billion Barrels of Venezuela’s Oil
nyt.description: The president said an agreement between the countries covered more than 65 billion barrels of reserves. A U.S. official said it would involve a partnership with a private company.

nyt.title: For Trump, the Iran War Is Stuck Between Combat and Genuine Peace
nyt.description: The war has deteriorated over the past six months into Mr. Trump’s own version of a “forever war,” with no clear goals and no end in sight.

nyt.title: ‘Lake America’? These Upstate New Yorkers Aren’t Letting Go of ‘Ontario.’
nyt.description: President Trump on Thursday signed an order rechristening Lake Ontario as Lake America, but businesses around Niagara Falls say they won’t be changing their tune.

nyt.title: Judge Rules Trump Unlawfully Targeted Stanford Students Who Criticized Israel
nyt.description: The ruling was a win for Stanford’s student newspaper, The Stanford Daily, and it followed another court victory for students targeted by the Trump administration last year.

nyt.title: Political Campaigns Are Quietly Paying Influencers to Support Candidates
nyt.description: Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.

nyt.title: In Georgia, Jon Ossoff Courts Broad Appeal With an Anti-Trump Script for Senate Race
nyt.description: Senator Jon Ossoff, the youngest sitting senator and the only Democrat seeking re-election this year in a state President Trump won in 2024, hasn’t moderated his message in his critical race.

nyt.title: High Debt and Rising Prices Catch Up to Trump, as Midterms Near
nyt.description: To win in 2024, the president promised an economic course correction. Almost two years later, his agenda has made that fight even harder.

nyt.title: One Democrat to Face Three Republicans for Alaska Governor
nyt.description: The second-place finisher in a primary where the top four advance to the November ballot said he would drop out of the race so voters could coalesce behind a single Democratic candidate.

nyt.title: Search Continues for 2,400 Missing in Nepal Floods Amid ‘Immense’ Devastation
nyt.description: As rescue efforts entered their fourth day, the scale of destruction came into focus, signaling a daunting recovery for the vulnerable nation.

nyt.title: Catastrophic Flood Exposes the Risks of Nepal’s Hydropower Bet
nyt.description: The loss of power-generating capacity has raised questions about an ambitious expansion of renewable energy in one of the world’s most hazard-prone mountain regions.

nyt.title: Nepali City Struggles to Handle the Many Bodies on Its Riverbanks
nyt.description: The remains of hundreds of people have washed downstream after devastating floods.

nyt.title: 37 Killed After Russian Strike on Weapons Depot as Ukraine Blames Negligence
nyt.description: The depot, which was in a civilian area near Kyiv, “definitely shouldn’t have been there,” President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

nyt.title: Unstable Manhattan Building Had More Damaged Columns Than Previously Known
nyt.description: Drawings obtained by The New York Times and reviewed by engineers show insufficient reinforcements on eight more steel columns than previously known at a Manhattan building.

nyt.title: Ina Garten Says You Can Either Get on Her Train or Get Out of the Way
nyt.description: At 78, the cookbook author and Food Network host knows what she likes, knows what she wants and isn’t stopping anytime soon.

nyt.title: Goodbye, Harry and Meghan. Turns Out We Didn’t Need Actual Royals.
nyt.description: With their departure, can America please shake off its obsession with royalty?

nyt.title: Democrats Have an Identity Politics Problem. Just Not the One You Think.
nyt.description: Instead of rallying around their candidates, Democrats are falling out among themselves.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Stand with Canada Against Trump
proj-syn.description: Rather than keeping their heads down as US President Donald Trump wages another trade war with Canada, European leaders must recognize that they could be next. Like Canada, the European Union is a middle power whose future prosperity and security will depend on solidarity with economic peers.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South?
proj-syn.description: The United States is an overextended hegemon, and its decline will continue slowly, as other powers like China assume more global responsibilities. Against this backdrop, China’s efforts to lead the Global South are more about consolidating its power in the current international system than creating a new one that benefits all.

proj-syn.title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
proj-syn.description: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. To dominate the industries of the future, they must learn from their own history and rebuild the institutions, expertise, and discipline that effective industrial policy demands.

proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins
proj-syn.description: Even if the AI investment boom turns out to have been a bubble, the Big Tech companies that have cornered the cloud infrastructure market will emerge as strong as ever, or even stronger. That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Mess With Markets
proj-syn.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has justified his intervention in currency and bond markets by arguing that they are not providing a fair signal of economic fundamentals. But they are, and Bessent's willingness to peddle such nonsense may be the most striking testament yet to the sycophancy that defines the Trump administration.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh Owes Us an Apology
proj-syn.description: After only a few months in office, the chair of the US Federal Reserve has left market participants disoriented and confused. His first address to the annual monetary-policy symposium in Jackson Hole is an opportunity to set things aright—or to make matters even worse.

proj-syn.title: Is the Trump Treasury Panicking?
proj-syn.description: With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt surpassing $40 trillion, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious. By trying to strong-arm the bond market rather than address the underlying problem, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may have squandered his hard-earned credibility.

proj-syn.title: What the World’s Oldest Bank Reveals About EU Financial Integration
proj-syn.description: To fend off an attempted takeover, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena has launched its own bids for two other Italian banks. The episode shows why EU policymakers should focus less on making governments surrender their influence over national banking systems and more on building a European financing channel.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.
